ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 3-bit Gray counter, with output terminals labeled A2, A1, and A0. A2 and A1 are respectively connected to the select terminals of the 4×1 MUX, corresponding to S1S0 = A2A1 according to the wiring in the figure; A0 is connected to the active-low enable terminal \bar{E} of the multiplexer. On the left side of the MUX are inputs I0, I1, I2, and I3, and on the right side is the output terminal. The output terminal is pulled up to +5V through resistor R, so when the MUX is not enabled, the output is high level 1. Reasoning: Starting from the initial state 000, the 8 states of the 3-bit Gray counter are, in order, 000, 001, 011, 010, 110, 111, 101, 100. For each state, if A0=1, then \bar{E}=1, the active-low enable is invalid, and the MUX output is pulled up to 1; if A0=0, then the MUX is enabled, the select terminals S1S0=A2A1, and the selection relationship is 00->I0, 01->I1, 11->I3, 10->I2. Therefore: 000 selects I0; 001 outputs 1; 011 outputs 1; 010 selects I1; 110 selects I3; 111 outputs 1; 101 outputs 1; 100 selects I2. Thus the output sequence is I0, 1, 1, I1, I3, 1, 1, I2.

method.method_draft: First list the eight Gray-counter states starting at 000. For each state, take A0 as E-bar: if A0=1, record output 1 due to pull-up. If A0=0, take S1S0=A2A1 from the same state and map 00->I0, 01->I1, 11->I3, 10->I2 as the enabled states occur. Reading across the Gray sequence gives I0, 1, 1, I1, I3, 1, 1, I2.

method.method_draft: Create a table indexed by all possible counter states A2A1A0. Fill it by the formula: Y=1 for odd states with A0=1; for A0=0, Y=I0 at 000, I1 at 010, I2 at 100, and I3 at 110.
